## P1.6 — Atomic quota and file revisions

Implementation and all declared Validation carriers are complete. Independent whole-item review: Grok 4.7/high, native 500000 context. Final correction verification is recorded separately in grok-review.md.

## Delivered

- Positive head-byte reservations use one conditional UPDATE on the Vaulter connection. Unlimited and exact-boundary quotas work; a rejected reservation rolls back metadata. Releases clamp at zero.
- Upload stages once, then takes drive → nodes → file → quota → CAS locks. Revisions read the locked file head and counter; repointHead records the allocated number. FileVersionStoreRepository::nextVersionNo is removed; document counters remain untouched.
- commitStaged commits reusable prepared bytes without discarding them. commit wraps stage/commitStaged/finally-discard; upload owns its staged object across three-attempt transaction retries. Promotion remains an idempotent saga with orphan reconciliation after grace.
- Copies lock a frozen source subtree and destination in id order, use current heads and reserve the complete summed delta atomically. Quota failure rolls back all copied rows and edges. The source membership stays fixed while new copy rows are inserted.
- V02, V03, V20 and V21, a separate aggregate-lock race, nonseekable-stream retry, copy/dedup-upload overlap without an outer retry, stale-head/stale-copy and staged-rollback tests are included.
- Public API golden, both guides, UPGRADE and Unreleased changelog are updated.

## Current validation

All records in validation.json have exit 0. Earlier failures remain in validation-initial.json and their original logs.

- Final drive PostgreSQL concurrency: five consecutive runs, each 17 passed, 547 assertions, zero failed and zero skipped. V21 runs ten move/upload iterations and measures at most two top-level attempts per operation (one retry).
- V02 negative control: replacing the conditional reservation with adjustUsedBytes makes both uploads succeed and the test fail. V03 negative control: removing aggregate FOR UPDATE causes duplicate (file_id, version_no) in each of five runs. Both source files were restored byte-for-byte before positive checks.
- The V03 upload path already has a node lock, which also serializes revisions. Its separate repository race tests file-counter allocation without that caller node lock; this makes the aggregate-lock negative control meaningful.
- SQLite quota feature tests: 7 passed. They cover NULL quota, exact boundary, +1 byte rejection, release/zero, entire-copy rollback, stale revision head and stale copy head.
- PostgreSQL media/Cas: 142 passed, 620 assertions; four inherited SQLite-specific skips. SQLite staged-commit delta: 3 passed.
- Core gate: Pint/PHPStan exit 0; Pest 662 passed, 28 inherited skips, 17 inherited risky annotations. Drive/documents/media/filament gates exit 0. Their SQLite PG-only skips and existing risky annotations are retained and are not claimed as executed.
- Code Guidance: adjustUsedBytes in drive source only in purge and negative upload delta; no file nextVersionNo in core/drive. Scoped whitespace check passes; unrelated roadmap EOF whitespace is untouched.

## Repairs and review

The specification's core repository reference to the Drive quota exception violates the adopted core → drive dependency-direction guard. The first core arch run reproduced this. A common core exception now owns the error; Drive Actions translate it to the existing Drive exception, preserving its public factory, message and HTTP 413 quota_exceeded response. Full core architecture and package gates pass without weakening tests. This is a bounded repair within the affected core/drive packages.

The first media PG run rejected the new staged-test fixture's nonnumeric drive id in a bigint column. The fixture now uses global scope, and the complete PG CAS suite passes.

One full review packet provided 73 complete files, all scoped changes, the item and OPUS requirements. The initial report is retained in grok-review-first.md. Its documentation residue was fixed. A same-session correction packet supplies the final changed sources, the missing connection/resumable-upload dependencies, UPGRADE, measured V21 attempt bounds and all final checks; its report is grok-review.md. Review is static; the reviewer did not rerun automated tests. Same-session correction verification is GREEN. Its last class-comment residue in CommitUploadAction is repaired without changing executable tokens; review-comment-fix.json records that bounded delta.

The suspected copy-FK/quota/CAS lock cycle did not reproduce. The baseline overlap test passed: PostgreSQL CAS uses advisory locks and plain blob row reads, while MySQL serializes same-storage writers through the tree row. No product lock-order change was made for that unproved hypothesis. The overlap regression remains in the suite.

## Scope and boundaries

Changed packages: core, drive and media, as explicitly selected by P1.6. Documents and filament were validated only. Adding the common core quota exception, preserving the Drive boundary and UPGRADE are necessary architecture/public-contract repairs. No document revision-counter changes, schema migrations, production mutations, push or release.

Tests used in-memory SQLite and the isolated native PostgreSQL vaulter_test database with fake local disks. MySQL concurrency was source-inspected, not exercised. The classified P1.7 MySQL installation deviation remains with its owning item. Phase-wide hosted CI requires owner gate O-3-CI and was not run by this item. P1.6 completion does not claim P1 phase closure.

Previously dirty configuration, plan source, journal and generated plan carriers stay in the owner's worktree; shared bookkeeping is left unstaged. Product changes, P1.6-owned evidence and clean-baseline handoff are the scoped commit.
